notable_absence.finding: This page dates exactly two of its seven optimizations - index projection to 5.0 and skip-key range scan to 6.5 - and dates none of predicate pushdown, composite predicate pushdown, pagination pushdown, order pushdown, or any of the four operator pushdowns. The order-pushdown limitation is dated only by the word 'Currently' ('Currently the Query engine supports order pushdown only when the ORDER BY keys are aligned with the Index order'), which is undatable and does not survive being extracted. More pointedly, version information has been REMOVED between releases: the 7.2 copy of this page said 'Prior to Couchbase Server 5.5, MAX() could be pushed to the Indexer only when the index was created with matching index keys in descending order. This limitation has been removed in Couchbase Server 5.5 and later' (and the mirror sentence for MIN()), which the 8.0 page has rewritten to the undated 'You do not need to create the index with the matching index keys sorted in descending order to push MAX() to the Indexer.' So version:server-5-5 is no longer attested anywhere on this page, and an 8.0-only reader cannot tell that MIN()/MAX() pushdown was ever conditional. Second absence, of a different kind: the page never says that grouping and aggregate pushdown is a member of the pushdown family. It appears only as a Related Links entry, even though the plan output in Examples 11, 12, 14 and 16 shows that MIN/MAX/COUNT pushdown is implemented through the same index_group_aggs plan field that groupby-aggregate-performance.md documents. Third: no vector indexes. An 8.0 page enumerating what the Indexer can be asked to do never mentions the three vector index types or vector search, so nothing here says whether any pushdown applies to them.

cross_component_finding: Three findings, all about which component is credited with the work. (1) An internal contradiction in the page's own output. Example 14's callout (1) reads 'The index operator IndexCountScan3 counts values so the Query Service does not need to do additional processing' and Example 16's reads the same for distinct values - but callout (1) in both examples points at a line of plan output that says "#operator": "IndexScan3", and IndexCountScan3 appears nowhere in any plan on the page. Either the plans were regenerated from a version that no longer uses IndexCountScan3 and the callouts were not updated, or the callouts describe an operator the examples do not actually produce. This is the same shape of defect as a title/content mismatch and it is duplicated, so it is unlikely to be a typo. (2) The page names its two components four different ways in one document: 'Query engine' (throughout), 'Query Service' (the two IndexCountScan3 callouts), 'query layer' (the pagination-pushdown factors), and 'Query nodes' / 'Indexer nodes' (the two-point rationale at the top), while the Indexer is 'the Indexer', 'the indexer' and 'Query Indexer'. The sibling page early-filters-and-pagination.md consistently says 'Index service' and 'Query service'. Anything downstream that keys on component names sees five spellings of two services across two pages of one module. (3) A namespace fork the corpus already had and this page makes visible: the four operator pushdowns are attested as n1ql:max-pushdown and n1ql:min-pushdown (server/7.2 round) while their family term is index:operator-pushdown and skip-key range scan is n1ql:skip-key-range-scan while its family term is index:composite-predicate-pushdown. I reused the existing n1ql: ids rather than fork them and minted the two new siblings (n1ql:count-pushdown, n1ql:count-distinct-pushdown) into the same namespace to keep the set countable, but round 16's rule ('index: for anything else true of indexes - settings, storage modes, rebalance methods, pushdowns, scan mechanics') says all six belong in index:. That is one deliberate move over six ids for phase 2, not six independent judgement calls.
